item.title: Thursday’s local roundup: Tyler Bourgea (3 goals), Tewksbury win 16th game
item.description: It was a Sweet 16 day for the Tewksbury High boys hockey team. The Redmen remained undefeated (16-0-1) on Thursday with a dominant 6-0 MVC/DCL Div. 2 victory over North Andover at the Breakaway Ice Center in Tewksbury. Tewksbury (9-0-1 in league play) held a commanding 50-8 shots advantage. Owen Sovie posted the eight-save shutout. […]

item.title: Pedestrian seriously injured after being struck by Lowell Police cruiser
item.description: LOWELL — A pedestrian was airlifted with serious injuries on Thursday evening after being struck by a Lowell Police cruiser while crossing Wilder Street on UMass Lowell's South Campus.

item.title: Behind the Bylines: Layoffs at The Post are a matter of public consequence
item.description: This week, The Washington Post announced massive layoffs. In a seemingly perpetually shrinking news industry, it would be easy to brush this off as another expected casualty. However, it should not be treated that casually. When a flagship newsroom experiences such a drastic loss, that loss reverberates beyond the institution and the industry itself.
